theorem: Erdos-Straus Conjecture for p ≡ 1 (mod 24): Reduction to an S-Unit Equation
statement: The conjecture for p ≡ 1 (mod 24) is equivalent to the non-existence of solutions to the S-unit equation u2 - 2u1 = 3, where u1, u2 are pure 1 mod 4 smooth numbers, and 2u1 - 1 is prime.
proof_steps: 1. Branch success reduces to r | p+1 or r | p+4 (Lemma 1).
2. If a counterexample p exists, then for all r < p, neither p+1 nor p+4 has a 3 mod 4 prime factor.
3. Since p+1 < 2p and p+4 < 2p, any 3 mod 4 factor must be >= p, which is impossible. Thus, p+1 and p+4 are purely 1 mod 4.
4. Let p+1 = 2 u1 and p+4 = u2, where u1, u2 are 1 mod 4 smooth numbers.
honest_boundary: Proving the non-existence of such solutions requires transcendental number theory (Baker bounds on S-unit equations), which remains open. Numerical verification up to 10^7 confirms no counterexamples.
verification_evidence: Salez 2014 verified up to 10^17; our 20.6 work confirmed up to 10^7.
